claims.text: The starting alloy is analogous to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 and is produced by conventional arc melting.
Introducing approximately 2–4 at.% boron during synthesis will improve glass-forming ability in the phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy.
Introducing approximately 2–4 at.% boron will improve the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
Boron addition will promote localized boron–phosphorus-enriched clusters in the amorphous matrix.
The boron–phosphorus-enriched clusters will form highly connected regions in the amorphous matrix.
Boron acts as a network former in this alloy.
Boron establishes strong directional bonds with phosphorus.
The enhanced short-range order frustrates atomic rearrangements required for crystallization.
Increased network connectivity raises the energy barrier for crystal nucleation.
The proposed mechanism lowers the critical cooling rate required to form an amorphous phase.
The boron-containing alloy will have a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature than the boron-free baseline.
The proposed benefit is expected during rapid melt spinning at cooling rates of 10^5–10^6 K/s under an inert atmosphere.
Boron contents above the optimal range may promote crystalline boride formation.
Formation of brittle crystalline borides would negate the desired improvements.

contradictions.description: The initial Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 composition already totals 100 at.%, while the modified alloy is specified only as receiving 2–4 at.% B. The baseline is described as having the same composition but no B, so the hypothesis does not state which original constituents are displaced or how they are renormalized; the two alloys therefore cannot literally have the same full composition.
